title: Preschool safety violations, enforcement transparency and parent notification
asked: Whether ECDA will introduce measures to make preschool safety violations and enforcement actions more transparent, whether parents can access preschools' safety records and ECDA's regulatory actions, and what safeguards ensure parents are told when serious safety violations happen at their child's preschool.
response: ECDA takes a serious view of child safety and will act against errant operators, including revoking a licence where breaches are severe and systemic. Preschools must notify parents immediately of serious incidents or illness affecting their child and report these to ECDA. ECDA publishes statements on serious safety violations and enforcement actions but generally does not name the preschools, to protect the identities of children involved, especially where court gag orders apply. Parents can judge a preschool by its licence tenure, displayed prominently and on LifeSG, where a 24-month licence means all key licensing requirements were met and a six-month licence means several areas for improvement.

key_points.point: ECDA may revoke a preschool's licence where breaches are severe and systemic.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: revoking the preschool's licence where breaches are severe and systemic

key_points.point: Preschools must notify parents immediately of a serious incident or illness affecting their child, and report it to ECDA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: preschools are also required to notify parents immediately when there is a serious incident or illness that affects their child

key_points.point: ECDA does not generally name the preschools, to protect the identities of children involved.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: ECDA does not generally name the preschools, to ensure that the identities of children involved are protected

key_points.point: Parents can use a centre's licence tenure to make informed decisions about preschools.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Parents can make informed decisions about preschools by considering the centre's licence tenure

key_points.point: A 24-month licence indicates a centre has met all key licensing requirements; a six-month licence indicates several areas for improvement.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: a 24-month licence indicates that a centre has met all key licensing requirements

key_points.point: On the 2023 incident, the Minister said he did not have the details and could not respond to that case.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: I do not have the details of the incident and cannot respond to this case.

key_points.point: Where there is no gag order and it is in the interest of parents and the public to know, ECDA will make a deliberate decision on releasing information.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we will make a deliberate decision whether or not to release such information

key_points.point: A recent addition to requirements is closed-circuit television installation in centres.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: A most recent addition was the requirement for closed-circuit television to be installed in the centres.
